project_metadata.job_title: I want to publish my paperback book. I am looking for an editor who can help me polish my manuscript
project_metadata.job_description:
I have a manuscript which I would like to publish as a paperback. Its around 8K words. This book is related to new parents. I can give more insight once we connect further.

I am new to publishing world. As you are working as an editor, could you help me in clarifying the steps needed for me to successfully publish this as a paperback ? 

Let me know if you would be interested in this task.

Thanks,
Puja

Hello Rakhi, thank you for the reply.

I am a mother and this book is written from my experiences as well as borrowed experiences. My book is about how new parents can set boundaries without awkward conversations and how visitors can behave around a newborn and new parents. Its a guide that answers the question every new Indian parent is too exhausted to answer - 'When can you visit, how long can you stay, and please don't kiss my baby.' I have added checklists, Do's & Don'ts tables, and some anecdotes. This is my first time as an author and I would appreciate your help with getting this paperback published successfully. Basically I would need help in fine-tuning the book which would be a delight to readers and in successfully publishing this book.

Could you please help me with the below:
1\. How should we go about it ?
2\. Also, what would be the price and timelines for this ?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Thank you for reviewing the manuscript and accepting the edits. I also noticed the highlighted sections, so no worries I’ll review those carefully while preparing the final version.

Regarding your questions:

1\. The sentence "So, I used to eat before anyone or sometimes after everytime, basically it was on demand." isn't grammatically natural. I'd suggest:

"So, I ate whenever I was hungry. Sometimes I ate before everyone else, and sometimes afterwards. My meals were completely on demand."

This keeps your meaning while making it read much more smoothly.

2\. You're absolutely right. The current wording reads as though you wished those things had happened, rather than describing your actual experience. Since you're sharing your own story, I'd suggest something like:

"The thing I needed most from my partner was not grand gestures. He answered the door when visitors arrived. He made sure my water bottle was always filled and within my reach. Sometimes he would simply check in on me, give me a hug, or put a blanket over me. He managed the visitors so I didn't have to. They were small acts, but they meant everything."

This clearly conveys that these were things your partner actually did for you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
1\. My honest opinion: I genuinely enjoyed reading your manuscript. I think you've addressed a topic that isn't talked about enough, especially in Indian families. Your writing feels warm, relatable, and easy to read, and I believe many new parents will see themselves in your experiences. If I had one suggestion, it would only be to tighten a few repetitive sections in a future edition. Overall, I think it's a lovely and genuinely helpful book.

2\. About images: Personally, I'd keep them minimal. A few simple illustrations or icons at the beginning of chapters would look great, but I wouldn't add too many. The writing itself is the highlight, and I think a clean, elegant layout will make it feel more professional.
